record.paper_title: Computational issues for linear periodic systems: paradigms, algorithms, open problems
record.original_question: For discrete-time linear periodic systems, can one develop an algorithm that computes an inner-outer factorization in the non-standard case? The desired method should work directly for periodic systems rather than only through lifted reductions, and it should be computationally satisfactory for periodic-system settings.

evidence.quote: For discrete-time systems, we mention the lack of algorithms for computing inner–outer factorisation (in the non-standard case)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time linear periodic system of period $K\ge 1$ with state-space realization
$$x_{k+1}=A_k x_k + B_k u_k,\qquad y_k=C_k x_k + D_k u_k,$$
where the matrix sequences $\{A_k\},\{B_k\},\{C_k\},\{D_k\}$ are $K$-periodic (i.e., $A_{k+K}=A_k$, etc.) and may have time-varying dimensions. Let $G$ denote the corresponding periodic input–output operator on $\ell_2$. An inner–outer factorization of $G$ is a representation $G = G_i G_o$ in which $G_i$ is a $K$-periodic inner operator (i.e., $G_i^\sim G_i = I$, with $G_i^\sim$ the conjugate operator) and $G_o$ is a $K$-periodic outer operator (i.e., causal with a causal pseudo-inverse on the range). The factorization is said to be "standard" when the periodic feedthrough matrices $D_k$ have full row (or column) rank uniformly in $k$ and $G$ has no zeros on the unit circle; otherwise it is "non-standard" (e.g., rank-deficient or singular feedthrough, zeros on the unit circle, or zeros at infinity).

Problem. Devise an algorithm that, for the general non-standard case, computes an inner–outer factorization $G = G_i G_o$ of an arbitrary discrete-time $K$-periodic system, returning $K$-periodic state-space realizations of the inner factor $G_i$ and the outer factor $G_o$. The algorithm must operate intrinsically on the periodic data $\{(A_k,B_k,C_k,D_k)\}_{k=0}^{K-1}$ — without reducing the problem to a single time-invariant lifted system — and must be numerically reliable and efficient with computational cost comparable to other state-of-the-art periodic-system algorithms (e.g., based on periodic QR/QZ-type orthogonal transformations and periodic Riccati/Schur computations).
artifact.status_search_result: Varga and collaborators have developed periodic coprime and inner–outer factorization algorithms for the standard square case (e.g., periodic right coprime factorization with inner denominator, PRCFID). Extensions handling time-varying dimensions and singular feedthrough matrices in the discrete-time periodic non-standard setting have been discussed, using deflation-based approaches analogous to Oară–Varga (1999), but a fully general, numerically reliable, intrinsically periodic algorithm for the non-standard case does not appear to be definitively settled in the literature.

status_evidence.title: On computing periodic coprime factorizations
status_evidence.snippet: For square periodic systems with invertible direct feedthrough matrices, the PRCFID algorithm can be used to compute an inner–outer factorization.
status_evidence.claim: Periodic inner-outer factorization is addressed only for the standard (invertible feedthrough) case via PRCFID.

status_evidence.title: The general inner–outer factorization problem for discrete-time systems
status_evidence.snippet: A computational solution to the general inner-outer factorization problem for discrete-time systems is based on descriptor state-space computations.
status_evidence.claim: General (non-standard) inner-outer factorization is solved for time-invariant discrete-time systems but the periodic counterpart is not fully developed.

status_evidence.title: Solutions to the General Inner–Outer and Spectral Factorization Problems (Varga, CDC 1998)
status_evidence.snippet: General inner–outer and spectral factorization for standard (non-periodic) systems.
status_evidence.claim: General-case algorithms exist for non-periodic systems but their direct extension to periodic systems is the open issue.
